_: ANTIGRAVITY CLI (agy) PERMISSIONS - the capability-denial layer, and the one an implementing agent cannot talk its way past. Merge into the settings used for implementation sessions: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json, or the project-scoped settings your build reads. VERIFY THE RULE GRAMMAR BEFORE TRUSTING THIS FILE: run `/permissions` in agy, add one of these denies through the TUI, then read the file back - the TUI is the authority on the exact syntax your build accepts, and it has changed between releases. `/permissions list` shows what is actually in force. Precedence is deny > ask > allow, and path matching is recursive, so a denied directory covers everything under it.
__toolPermission: request-review is the default and is the right mode here. Do NOT use strict: it denies all non-read operations, and the implementer's whole job is writing driver code. proceed-in-sandbox pairs well with Tier 1 - auto-approve inside the sandbox, ask outside it - if you want an implementer that runs unattended.
__note_web: search_web and read_url_content are denied outright: every citable reference is pre-fetched into docs/references/ by the orchestrator, so an implementation session never needs the network. This is also what stops the model from routing around a blocked path by reading a code-browser mirror.
__note_paths: Edit the checkout paths to match your machine and keep them in sync with cleanroom-policy.json. Better still, don't mount an encumbered checkout in the implementation workspace at all - a path that isn't there needs no rule.
__note_scoping: These rules apply to whatever session reads this settings file, and CLEANROOM_ROLE means nothing to them. The dirty side (investigator/verifier) must therefore run from settings WITHOUT these denies - a separate agy invocation, not the same session.
